messages:
jessica: Heads-up — over the last 90m we've seen intermittent packet loss affecting model-serving pods on gpu-node pools A/B. Symptoms: grpc stream resets, 95/99th latency spikes, and occasional failed healthchecks during autoscale. Pattern looks like east-west only (pod→pod on different hosts).

pagerduty-bot: [ALERT] service/model-serving-high-error-rate triggered for cluster: prod-eu-gpu (count: 18, window: 10m)

oliver: Thanks — I grabbed tcpdump+ss on one pair. Quick notes: flow shows repeated retransmits and some large geneve packets getting ICMP frag-needed from a downstream hypervisor. suspect PMTU blackhole when geneve adds ~50B.

samir: Can you paste the tcpdump snippet? also what's host MTU and pod MTU? geneve vni size?

jessica: snippet:```17:42:11.123456 IP 10.244.5.12.50052 > 10.244.7.8.50052: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12800, ack 54321, win 29200, length 455``` then later: ```ICMP 192.168.1.1 unreachable - need to frag (mtu 1500)``` Host NIC MTU=9000, pod netns veth mtu=1500, geneve on hosts uses mtu 8900.

oliver: Huh — host MTU is jumbo but somewhere along path a middlebox/hypervisor expects 1500. Geneve+GSO can produce large UDP frames that get dropped if intermediate doesn't handle UDP GSO. On mlx5 boxes we also saw offload counters incrementing.

samir: Confirmed mismatch: some compute racks still on older TOR that rewrites/generates ICMP frag-needed without honoring UDP GSO segmentation. Kernel versions differ (5.10 vs 5.15) across pools too. That combo + RDMA (mlx5) seems to trigger weird GRO/GSO behavior for encapsulated flows.

katy: Immediate mitigations to try (canary first):
- enable TCP/UDP MTU probing: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1`
- temporarily disable GSO/GRO/TSO on overlay veths for affected nodes:
```
for if in $(ip -o link | awk -F': ' '{print $2}' | grep -E "^veth|^kube-" ); do
  ethtool -K $if gro off gso off tso off || true
done
```
- set geneve device mtu to 1450 on hosts where downstream is 1500-limited: `ip link set geneve0 mtu 1450`
- as a short term kube-svc: annotate pods to prefer same-host scheduling for heavy streaming until fixed

oliver: I'll roll the GSO disable to two canaries in eu-west-1 and run iperf3 between pods with `-M 1200` to force smaller MSS. Also will enable tcp_mtu_probing cluster-wide if it looks OK.

samir: Long-term: push kernel 5.15+ to unify behavior, update NIC FW/driver (mlx5) — there are known fixes around UDP GSO with encapsulation. Also consider using vxlan (UDP) vs geneve? Both suffer but drivers have different fast-paths. We should also add a probe that simulates encapsulated large UDP + mtu to detect blackholes proactively.

jessica: I already applied the geneve mtu=1450 on 2 canaries and disabled gso/gro on the veths. Initial smoke: grpc resets dropped from ~8/min to 0-1/min on canary.

katy: Nice. Can you collect `ethtool -k` and `dmesg` outputs and attach to the incident ticket? also tag networking oncall.

oliver: Copying commands I ran for reproducible triage:
```
# capture with timestamps
sudo timeout 30 tcpdump -i any -w /tmp/geneve-trace.pcap '(udp and port 6081) or host 10.244.7.8'
# iperf test (from pod netns)
iperf3 -c 10.244.7.8 -u -b 500M -M 1200 -t 20
# check offloads
ethtool -k eth0
# offload counters
cat /sys/kernel/debug/mlx5/port*/counters
```

samir: FYI I saw kernel message on one host: `mlx5_core 0000:3b:00.0: UDP GSO: unsupported encapsulation, falling back` followed by `NETDEV WATCHDOG: veth12345 stuck` — indicates driver/kernel interaction.

jessica: Plan: finish canary soak (30m), if stable apply to remaining nodes in the pool, then schedule driver/firmware upgrade for next maintenance window. Open followup to add MTU/encap blackhole synthetic check to our cluster health probes.

katy: +1. Also add a note in the GPU capacity runbook: when autoscale moves pods cross-rack, MTU/encap mismatches can surface — include mitigations.

jessica: will update ticket and ping infra-runbook. thanks all :thumbsup:
